### Meditate with Me on Isaiah 42:21
Author: John Piper
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/meditate-with-me-on-isaiah-42-21
Passage: Isaiah 42:21
Points:
- God's righteousness compels Him to magnify and uphold the honor of His own instruction.
- Divine righteousness is defined by God's infinite worth, making it right for Him to exalt His word.
- God acts in complete freedom because He genuinely delights to do what is right.
- In God's nature, practicing righteousness and experiencing holy joy are inseparable.
- Believers redeemed by Christ are transformed to find true freedom in joyfully doing what is right.

### The Savior of God's Blind Servant
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/savior-gods-blind-servant
Passage: Isaiah 42:18–43:7
Points:
- The blind and deaf servant portrays fallen Israel suffering in exile because of their transgressions.
- Even amid severe plundering and defeat, the people remained oblivious to their own depravity.
- God sovereignly pledged not to abandon His people permanently in their spiritual blindness.
- Deliverance and restoration are acts of pure divine grace rather than human merit.
- God's gracious election of an unworthy people finds its ultimate fulfillment in Jesus Christ.
